drhp.business: Trident operates diversified business segments comprising Bed Linen, Bath Linen, Yarn, Paper and Chemicals, supported by a captive power plant that meets the internal power needs of its various business segments. It runs an integrated fibre-to-fabric textile ecosystem alongside a sustainable paper operation that makes high-speed printing and publishing paper, branded copier paper and wheat straw-based paper. The Company serves leading global retailers, brands, hospitality players, institutional buyers, printing and publishing customers and e-commerce platforms across more than 100 countries, …

risks.note: A significant share of revenue remains linked to global demand conditions and trade policies — exports contributed 53.73% of total sale in FY2025-26, so weakness in overseas retail demand or adverse tariff action transmits directly to the top line.

Global conflicts, shipping disruptions and changes in international trade policies may impact exports, supply chains and export competitiveness; management flagged trade barriers, geopolitical developments and supply-chain disruptions across several markets during the year.
Fluctuations in cotton, pulp, fuel chemicals and energy prices can affect margins; freight rate volatility and shipping disruptions can further impact costs and delivery timelines.

Operations in textiles and paper are energy-intensive and dependent on conventional energy sources; failure to mitigate Scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG emissions could expose the Company to carbon pricing mechanisms, carbon taxes and stricter emission reporting obligations, while India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) may raise compliance costs.

Manufacturing facilities are directly exposed to extreme heat waves, flooding and water scarcity that can disrupt plant operations and damage infrastructure; dependence on cotton as a primary raw material presents supply risk as erratic rainfall, prolonged droughts and rising temperatures drive up procurement costs.
risks.risk: Physical climate risk and cotton raw-material availability

risks.note: Sustained investments are required for technology upgrades, sustainability initiatives and capacity enhancement, while textile and paper operations consume significant energy, water and raw materials — exposing the Company to both reinvestment burden and evolving environmental compliance costs.
Competition from low-cost manufacturing nations may exert pricing pressure on Trident's export-facing textile businesses.

Large-scale manufacturing operations require continuous availability of skilled and technical talent; the turnover rate for permanent employees was 38.77% in FY2025-26 (40.57% in FY2024-25) and for permanent workers 22.23%.
risks.risk: Dependence on skilled workforce and attrition

The USA and the European Union are the primary export destinations, together making up approximately 47% of India's textile and apparel exports.
